title: Many chains
hook: some reports come through so many chains that they're certain

segments.voice: Yesterday, sahih, sound, and your line: graded with care. Did you find the grade of the hadith you chose, or someone to ask? Day one thousand one hundred forty-eight.

Have you ever stood in Antarctica? If not, can you prove it's there? Not with your own eyes. And yet nobody lies awake wondering whether it was invented. Explorers, scientists, maps, photographs, people who have no reason to agree with each other, all saying the same thing. At some point, doubting it would take more effort than believing it. Muslim scholars of law and hadith used this same kind of example, a far-off place you've never visited, to explain a special kind of knowing. Not a report from one person. A report from so many that it can't be a lie. Today, mutawatir.
screen: `A PLACE YOU'VE NEVER SEEN.` → `NOBODY DOUBTS IT.` → `NOT ONE REPORT. SO MANY.`

segments.voice: First, the word. A mutawatir report is one carried by so many people, at every step of its chain, that their agreeing on a falsehood is beyond belief. Not one chain. Many chains, running side by side, from the first generation down. Second, how many is so many? Here scholars differ, and say so. Some proposed a minimum number. Others said no fixed number works: what matters is that the crowd is large enough, and varied enough, that knowledge follows without effort, the way it does about that faraway place. Third, an example scholars give. The Prophet ﷺ said, in a report in both Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim: whoever tells a lie about me on purpose, let him take his seat in the Fire. Scholars describe that sentence as reaching them through companion after companion, by many roads. Notice the irony: a report carried this widely is a warning against inventing reports. Fourth, the contrast. Plenty of reports are not mutawatir. They come through one chain, or a few, and scholars call them ahad, solitary. That's not an insult. A solitary report can be sound, and acted on. But scholars of theology and law have discussed what kind of knowledge a single chain gives, and they don't all answer the same way. And something bigger: Muslim scholars describe the Qur'an itself as carried this way, recited aloud by crowds in every generation, not passed down a single line. So certainty, in this science, is not a feeling. It's a crowd that couldn't all have made it up.
screen: `MANY CHAINS, SIDE BY SIDE.` · `HOW MANY? SCHOLARS DIFFER.` · `A WARNING, WIDELY CARRIED.` · `AHAD: ONE CHAIN, OR A FEW.`

segments.voice: The practice: think about certainty. Settle, and breathe. Name three things you're sure of. One you saw yourself. One you know because a single person told you. And one you know because so many people said it, from so many directions, that you've never thought to doubt it. Hold each one up in turn. How do you know it? Which feels solid, and which feels solid but is really one voice? Don't rush to change your mind about anything. Just sort them. The bell holds the time.

Mutawatir. A report carried by so many, through so many chains, that it gives certain knowledge. It ends a week that opened with the weakest pillar and walked through hadith, sunnah, isnad, matn and sahih. Today's word.
Your line: so many said it. Today, when you're certain of something, ask whether it's one voice or many. Tomorrow: the science of men. Day one thousand one hundred forty-eight.

howItsDone: Scholars of hadith and legal theory distinguish mutawatir reports, carried by so many that they give certainty, from ahad reports carried by one or a few chains, and Muslims describe the Qur'an as transmitted by mass recitation in every generation.

fork.setup: you've never been to a far-off city, but travelers from everywhere, strangers to each other, describe it the same way. what do the scholars say you have?
fork.reveal: a crowd that couldn't all have agreed on a lie gives certain knowledge. that's the idea behind mutawatir.

original.note: a report carried by so many chains that it gives certainty.

trapdoor: what you thought: a hadith is certain if it's in a famous book.
what it means: only some reports come through so many chains that they're certain; others come through one or a few.
what a scholar hears: tawatur against ahad, and a debate in law and theology over what kind of knowledge a single chain gives.

notes: The hook uses Antarctica as a modern stand-in for the classical example (knowing that a distant city exists without having seen it); Confirm the classical example is described fairly.
'Many companions carried that sentence, by many roads' and 'an example scholars often reach for': the hadith is commonly cited as mutawatir; no number given. Confirm.
'A report carried this widely' describes the mutawatir status scholars give it; confirm.
'A great deal of hadith is not mutawatir': general; confirm.
'Scholars of theology and law have long discussed' whether ahad reports give certainty: general; confirm.
